findings.detail: Validation quorum is max(ceil(effectiveUNL*0.67), ceil(UNL*0.60)) (ValidatorList.cpp:1845-1935); consensus threshold minCONSENSUS_PCT is 67 (ConsensusParms.h:79); post-fix amendment threshold is 67/100 strictly greater (SystemParameters.h:85). Upstream docs say 80% for all three. A 7-of-10 side keeps validating where an 80% rule would stall it; the halt band is 33-67% faulty, not 20-80%.
findings.title: This fork uses 67% thresholds, not the documented 80%

findings.detail: With divergent UNLs (sizes 8 and 7, quorums 6 and 5), both sides quorum-validated all 40 ledgers; the heal discarded 40 validated ledgers. The code permits this under the Theorem 8 bound (ValidatorList.cpp:1898-1929).
findings.title: Dual validation is possible under UNL divergence (S-04)

findings.detail: No function, flag, RPC field, or log line named split-brain or fork-detection exists in the pinned code. The only 'divergence' hit is the untrusted-proposal drop (src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp:1865-1870). Detection is emergent: preferred-ledger comparison, quorum-gated validation advance, operating mode. The simulator defines 10 modelled signals; 46 fired across the scenarios.
findings.title: No explicit split-brain detector exists in the pinned code

findings.detail: In 7 of 10 scenarios the minority side closed ledgers but validated none (S-01: 40 closed / 0 validated; S-09: 200 / 0). Consensus keeps running via stalled/MovedOn/Expired exits; only validation stalls. Unvalidated ledgers accumulate silently and are discarded at heal.
findings.title: Minority sides close ledgers but never validate them

findings.detail: Each side counts only its own trusted validations. S-05: side A recorded tfGotMajority (7 yes > 4.69) at flag ledger 8283904; side B (3 trusted < quorum 7) did not vote at all and its amendment clock froze. There is no cross-partition reconciliation; the surviving majority timestamps are the winning chain's.
findings.title: Amendment clocks freeze below quorum; split majorities do not reconcile

findings.detail: The 2-week hold is 1,209,600 s of ledger close time; at the modelled 4 s/ledger it needs 302,400 ledgers. No amendment can activate inside any short partition in this pack.
findings.title: The 2-week amendment hold is unreachable inside short partitions

findings.detail: S-09 (200 ledgers, 800 s simulated): pre-partition validations crossed LOCAL at round 45 (180 s), WALL at round 75 (300 s), and the 10-minute set expiry at round 150 (600 s); all 3 pre-partition validation sets were swept. After round 150 the minority side holds no usable pre-partition validation.
findings.title: Validation-expiry cascade after 10 minutes (S-09)

findings.detail: 2 of 3 publishers unavailable reaches min(listThreshold_=2, 3-2+1=2), so calculateQuorum returns SIZE_MAX and nothing validates anywhere, although all 10 validators are connected and agree. S-08: 30 ledgers closed, 0 validated.
findings.title: Publisher outage freezes all validation without any partition (S-08)

findings.detail: S-03 (5 up / 5 down flapping, 60 ledgers): 30 ledgers validated (up windows only), 0 validated while down, no side ever validated alone, 25 ledgers discarded / 25 refetched across 5 reconvergences. The scenario honestly ends unreconciled (mid-down-window).
findings.title: Flapping links cost liveness without forking (S-03)

findings.detail: S-06 minority side: close-time votes disagree internally, no 75% close-time consensus, resolution coarsened 30 -> 60 -> 90 -> 120 s, and every ledger carries sLCF_NoConsensusTime (0x01). Majority side refined to 10 s. Close-time drift is an observable partition signal.
findings.title: Close-time drift is an observable partition signal (S-06)

findings.detail: Across all scenarios: 485 ledgers discarded, 515 refetched, 0 timeouts. Worst-case bound is (6+1) x 3 s = 21 s per ledger (InboundLedger.cpp:44-74, 366-413). Rejoin cost is bounded and small when peers hold the ledgers.
findings.title: Rejoin cost is bounded: 0 timeouts, 21 s per-ledger worst case

findings.detail: S-07: the isolated validator (0 peers < minPeerCount) is DISCONNECTED, closes 0 ledgers and validates nothing; the other 9 validate all 30. Rejoin refetches 30 ledgers with 0 discards. A single validator cannot fork the network.
findings.title: Single-validator isolation is safe: no fork, clean rejoin (S-07)
